meta.title: SustainableAI Score
meta.tagline: See how your AI stack really stacks up.
meta.description: A 6-dimension framework rating AI providers and tools on environmental and societal sustainability. Higher is better.

dimensions.label: Hardware & Manufacturing
dimensions.description: Supply chain ethics, conflict minerals, fab locations, forced labor risk, right to repair, e-waste takeback.

dimensions.label: Data Center Operations
dimensions.description: Grid carbon intensity where the compute runs, renewable matching quality, water use, community impact.

dimensions.label: Training Footprint
dimensions.description: Disclosed training compute and energy, dataset sourcing and consent, labeling labor conditions.

dimensions.label: Inference Efficiency
dimensions.description: Model size options, quantization, sparse architectures, local inference availability, per-query energy.

dimensions.label: Company Governance
dimensions.description: Open versus closed weights, published sustainability reporting, labor practices, litigation, lock-in.

dimensions.label: Tool/Agent Design
dimensions.description: Local-first capability, caching, model routing by task complexity, transparency about per-call cost.

insights.title: Transparency moved the needle
insights.body: Mistral published the first peer-reviewed life cycle assessment of an LLM and is the single largest mover in the table, climbing from Poor to Good. Disclosure alone lifted its score by seven points.

insights.title: Local plus solar is still unbeaten
insights.body: Running open weights on hardware you already own, on solar power, scores 28 of 30. No cloud provider comes within six points. It remains the biggest single lever available to an individual.

insights.title: The buildout is outrunning the grid
insights.body: Google's electricity use rose 37 percent in a single year, Microsoft's emissions rose 25 percent, and most planned US data centers sit on land that was in drought. Efficiency gains are being consumed by volume.

insights.title: Training disclosure is still the gap
insights.body: Almost every provider scores 1 or 2 on training footprint. Meta is the only one publishing GPU-hours and carbon for an open model line, and even its newest frontier models are closed with no disclosures.

insights.title: Regulation arrived, reporting has not
insights.body: The EU AI Act now requires general purpose model providers to document energy consumption, and the EU Energy Efficiency Directive mandates data center reporting. Most labs still publish nothing.

insights.title: xAI, now SpaceXAI, is the floor
insights.body: Unpermitted gas turbines grew from 27 to 69, the Department of Justice is fighting a Clean Air Act citizen suit on national security grounds, and it remains the thinnest climate discloser among frontier labs.

providers.name: Hermes CLI + Gemma 4 (local, solar)
providers.summary: Runs on hardware you already own, powered by home solar, with open-weight models you control.
providers.tradeoffs: Model quality caps at the 7B to 13B level versus frontier cloud models. Not suitable for every task, so keep a cloud option for complex research.
gaps: Smaller models mean lower quality on complex reasoning than cloud frontier models
No per-query energy tracking built into the tool chain

providers.name: Mistral AI
providers.summary: The most transparent lab in the set, with a published life cycle assessment and open weights on its flagship.
providers.tradeoffs: Mistral published the first comprehensive, peer-reviewed life cycle assessment of a large language model, covering carbon, water and resource depletion across training and inference, and it moved its flagship Mistral Large 3 to Apache 2.0. Inference is efficient and aimed at a low-carbon French grid. Offsetting that, there is still no annual sustainability report, no PUE or renewable-matching methodology, and training datasets are explicitly withheld.
gaps: No PUE, water use or renewable-matching methodology published for its own or partner data centers
No updated life cycle assessment for the current model line, and GPU counts rather than GPU-hours for training
Training datasets explicitly withheld as of August 2026
No supply chain ethics program: no conflict minerals policy, supplier locations, or e-waste takeback
The Saudi HUMAIN partnership hosts workloads on a fossil-heavy grid, partly offsetting the French advantage

providers.name: Meta (Llama)
providers.summary: Still the best training disclosure of any open model line, held back by gas fired growth and a thin supply chain story.
providers.tradeoffs: Llama 4 keeps peer-leading openness about training: architecture, data mix, 7.38 million H100-hours and 1,999 tonnes of CO2e. Meta has also signed genuine firm clean power including the Clinton nuclear plant and new nuclear agreements, and it shipped Muse Glimmer, a 30B model under Apache 2.0 that runs on a single consumer GPU. Against that, location based emissions rose 11 percent year on year, renewable matching is annual rather than hourly, and the 5 GW Hyperion buildout is gas heavy and under active litigation.
gaps: No per-query inference energy or carbon published for any Llama or Muse model
No full lifecycle carbon assessment for any model line
Frontier Muse Spark models are closed weight with no model card or training disclosures
Energy and water for leased and under construction data centers are not disclosed
Annual rather than hourly renewable matching, with no 24/7 carbon-free energy target

providers.name: Google DeepMind (Gemini)
providers.summary: Publishes the most detailed per-query impact data in the industry while its absolute footprint keeps climbing.
providers.tradeoffs: Google now publishes measured per-query serving impact for Gemini, roughly 0.24 Wh of energy and 0.26 mL of water for a median prompt, which no other frontier lab does, and its Ironwood TPUs claim large carbon efficiency gains. Water replenishment reached 78 percent of consumption and PUE is 1.09. But total ambition-based emissions rose 18 percent to about 14.47 million tonnes, electricity use rose 37 percent in a single year, 24/7 carbon-free energy has stalled near 65 percent, and copyright litigation over training data has intensified.
gaps: No disclosed training compute, energy or carbon for the Gemini line
24/7 carbon-free energy stalled near 65 percent against a 2030 target of 100 percent
Total ambition-based emissions up 18 percent year on year and 81 percent above the 2019 base year
Water consumption rose to about 10.87 billion gallons, with site level data only for owned facilities
No consumer facing per call energy or carbon indicator

providers.name: DeepSeek V4 Flash
providers.summary: Genuine efficiency leadership under MIT weights, still undermined by a coal heavy grid and zero footprint disclosure.
providers.tradeoffs: DeepSeek V4 sets a new efficiency bar: V4 Flash activates 13B of 284B parameters and cuts one million token context inference to 27 percent of the previous generation's FLOPs and 10 percent of its KV cache, with MIT licensed weights that make local deployment widespread. China's grid has also improved, with coal falling below half of generation. But the serving fleet is still carbon heavy, a new 1 GW Inner Mongolia campus raises absolute demand, and the company publishes no training energy, carbon, PUE or water data at all.
gaps: No training energy, carbon, PUE or water disclosure, and a zero score on training energy in the Stanford transparency index
Serving fleet remains roughly half coal, at about 511 gCO2 per kWh
The 1 GW Ulanqab campus is not expected online until late 2027, so today's serving stays carbon heavy
Efficiency claims rest on DeepSeek's own baseline, with no independent energy benchmark of V4
Censorship is embedded in the weights rather than applied at the app layer, and persists in self hosted deployments
State linked ownership and alleged military support and export control evasion

providers.name: Anthropic (Claude)
providers.summary: Real efficiency controls and a novel grid cost pledge, against an absence of any environmental reporting.
providers.tradeoffs: Model tiers plus an effort dial and prompt caching let you cut per-task energy, and Anthropic became the first AI lab to pledge covering 100 percent of grid upgrade costs and procuring net new generation for its data centers. It also joined the Frontier carbon removal coalition. But training and inference energy remain undisclosed, there is no sustainability report and no renewable energy target, and the models are closed weight and cloud only.
gaps: No training compute, energy or carbon published, and zero environmental impact disclosure in the Stanford transparency index
No sustainability report, greenhouse gas inventory, net zero target or renewable energy target
No water consumption disclosure anywhere
No public dataset card, and a finalized 1.5 billion dollar copyright settlement over pirated books
Closed weights and cloud only, with no local or quantized path
No per query energy disclosure

providers.name: Claude Desktop
providers.summary: Now lets you choose a model and bridge to local inference, but still ships a heavy sandbox and reports nothing.
providers.tradeoffs: The desktop app now exposes a model dropdown rather than defaulting to the largest model, and MCP extensions plus local model bridges make it possible to route some work to Ollama or LM Studio. That is a real improvement in tool design. It still reports no per call energy or cost, launches a roughly 1.8 GB sandbox virtual machine on every start even for chat only use, and inherits Anthropic's training opacity.
gaps: No per call or per task energy and cost transparency, only usage limit meters
Cloud only by default, with local inference available only through unofficial bridges
Model choice is manual rather than automatically routed by task complexity
Ships a roughly 1.8 GB sandbox virtual machine on every launch, even for chat
Inherits Anthropic's training opacity and discloses no environmental data

providers.name: OpenAI Codex CLI
providers.summary: Now a genuine hybrid agent with local models, sitting on the weakest disclosure of any major lab.
providers.tradeoffs: Codex CLI is the best designed open-source cloud coding agent and, since January 2026, it runs fully local open-weight models through Ollama and LM Studio, with model routing and prompt caching. Those tool and inference gains are real. The vendor behind it still publishes no sustainability report, no verified emissions and no training energy, while new capacity is increasingly gas fired and litigation keeps widening.
gaps: OpenAI still publishes no environmental or sustainability report, and no verified Scope 1, 2 or 3 emissions
No training compute, energy or carbon published for the GPT line
New Stargate capacity is gas heavy, with a 3.2 GW Georgia project drawing on roughly 5.8 GW of mostly gas generation
The Abilene campus consumed about 463 million gallons of water while local residents faced drought restrictions
Escalating litigation on copyright, safety and agent misuse
Data labeling labor conditions largely unchanged, with Kenyan workers reported at roughly $1.32 to $2 per hour
No conflict minerals, e-waste takeback or right to repair policy, including for the in-house Jalapeno inference chip

providers.name: xAI / SpaceXAI (Grok)
providers.summary: Unpermitted gas turbines, federal litigation, and the thinnest climate disclosure of any frontier lab.
providers.tradeoffs: The only genuine improvement is tool design: Grok Build was open sourced under Apache 2.0 with a local-first design, a real model ladder, and prompt caching. Everything else is negative. The unpermitted turbine fleet grew from 27 to 69 units, the Department of Justice intervened to fight a Clean Air Act citizen suit on national security grounds, and the company remains the thinnest discloser among frontier labs.

Department of Justice intervention to dismiss a Clean Air Act citizen suit, with a likely appeal

Five data centers in the Memphis and Southaven area with a 946 MW campus, and an aquifer withdrawal dispute
Environmental justice concerns: South Memphis is predominantly Black and low income
No resolution on the turbine removal timeline or the data center moratorium vote
